units.title: Overview of the digestive system
units.summary: Overview of Digestive System • A healthy digestive system is essential to maintain life because it converts foods into raw materials that build and fuel our cells. • Main functions of the digestive system • Ingestion • Digestion • Absorption Absorb molecules into the bloodstream • Egestion Rid body of any indigestible remains Overview of Digestive System • Organs of the digestive system fall into two groups: • (1) Alimentary canal (gastrointestinal or GI tract or gut • (2) Accessory digestive organs Overview of Digestive System • (1) Alimentary canal • Continuous muscular tube • From the mouth to anus • Peristalsis • Site of digesting food breaks down food into smaller molecules • Absorbs food molecules into blood/lymph • Organs • mouth • Stomach • small intestine • large intestine Overview of Digestive System • (2) Accessory digestive organs • Teeth • Tongue • Gallbladder • Digestive glands produce secretions that help break down food chemically • Salivary glands • Liver • Pancreas
summary_sentences: Overview of Digestive System • A healthy digestive system is essential to maintain life because it converts foods into raw materials that build and fuel our cells.
• Main functions of the digestive system • Ingestion • Digestion • Absorption Absorb molecules into the bloodstream • Egestion Rid body of any indigestible remains
Overview of Digestive System • Organs of the digestive system fall into two groups: • (1) Alimentary canal (gastrointestinal or GI tract or gut • (2) Accessory digestive organs

Overview of Digestive System • (1) Alimentary canal • Continuous muscular tube • From the mouth to anus • Peristalsis • Site of digesting food breaks down food into smaller molecules • Absorbs food molecules into blood/lymph • Organs • mouth • Stomach • small intestine • large intestine

Overview of Digestive System • (2) Accessory digestive organs • Teeth • Tongue • Gallbladder • Digestive glands produce secretions that help break down food chemically • Salivary glands • Liver • Pancreas

units.title: Basic structure of the alimentary canal
units.summary: Overview of Digestive System Basic Structure of Alimentary Canal • Walls of alimentary canal have the same four basic tissue layers • Mucosa • Epithelium that covers surface of lumen • Secretes mucus, digestive enzymes, and hormones • Absorbs end products of digestion • Protects against infectious disease • Submucosa • Connective tissue • Contains blood and lymphatic vessels, and nerve plexus • Muscularis externa • Inner circular layer and outer longitudinal layer of smooth muscle tissue for peristalsis • Serosa • Outermost connective tissue

units.title: Functional anatomy of the digestive system
units.summary: Anatomy of Digestive System • Mouth and Associated Organs • Mouth (Oral cavity / Buccal cavity) is where food is ingested, chewed, and mixed with saliva that begins process of digestion, and swallowing process is initiated • Associated organs include: • Tongue • Salivary glands • Teeth Name of Muscle Description Origin (O) Insertion (I) Action Muscles of Mastication (Self-Study Closes off nasopharynx during swallowing Teeth: Chewing to tear and grind food into smaller fragments 20 milk teeth 32 permanent teeth Gripping, positioning, and mixing of food during chewing Mixing food and saliva to form bolus Involving in swallowing, speech, and taste Closes off trachea during swallowing Functions of saliva ➢ Cleanses mouth ➢ Dissolves food chemicals for taste ➢ Moistens food; compacts into bolus ➢ Begins breakdown of starch with enzyme salivary amylase Anything that inhibits saliva secretion can promote tooth decay Lack of saliva also makes it difficult to talk and swallow Anatomy of Digestive System • Pharynx • Connects to esophagus and trachea • Allows passage of food, fluids, and air • Esophagus • Muscular tube that runs from pharynx to stomach • Peristalsis for squeezing bolus toward stomach • Secrete mucus to enhance bolus movement • Heartburn Discomfort burning sensation caused by stomach acid regurgitating into esophagus
summary_sentences: Anatomy of Digestive System • Mouth and Associated Organs • Mouth (Oral cavity / Buccal cavity) is where food is ingested, chewed, and mixed with saliva that begins process of digestion, and swallowing process is initiated • Associated organs include: • Tongue • Salivary glands • Teeth
Name of Muscle Description Origin (O) Insertion (I) Action Muscles of Mastication

(Self-Study Closes off nasopharynx during swallowing Teeth: Chewing to tear and grind food into smaller fragments 20 milk teeth 32 permanent teeth Gripping, positioning, and mixing of food during chewing Mixing food and saliva to form bolus Involving in swallowing, speech, and taste Closes off trachea during swallowing

Functions of saliva ➢ Cleanses mouth ➢ Dissolves food chemicals for taste ➢ Moistens food; compacts into bolus ➢ Begins breakdown of starch with enzyme salivary amylase Anything that inhibits saliva secretion can promote tooth decay Lack of saliva also makes it difficult to talk and swallow

Anatomy of Digestive System • Pharynx • Connects to esophagus and trachea • Allows passage of food, fluids, and air • Esophagus • Muscular tube that runs from pharynx to stomach • Peristalsis for squeezing bolus toward stomach • Secrete mucus to enhance bolus movement • Heartburn Discomfort burning sensation caused by stomach acid regurgitating into esophagus

units.title: Physiology of digestion and absorption
units.summary: Physiology of Digestion and Absorption • Chemical Digestion • Breaks down ingested foods into their chemical building blocks • Digestive enzymes are involved • Final end products are small enough to be absorbed across wall of small intestine • Absorption • Moves substances from lumen of gut into body • Most nutrients are absorbed before chyme reaches ileum • Passive and active ways of membrane transport are use Physiology of Digestion and Absorption • Digestive juices in small intestine • Bile • Produce by liver; Store by gallbladder; Release into duodenum • Contains bile acid and phospholipids for emulsifying lipids • Contains bicarbonate for neutralizing gastric acid • Other components: bile pigment, cholesterols, ions ○ Pancreatic juice • Produce by pancreas; Release into duodenum • Contains digestive enzymes for chemical digestion of carbohydrate, proteins, and lipids • Contains bicarbonate for neutralizing gastric acid Physiology of Digestion and Absorption Monosaccharides are absorbed into blood via facilitated diffusion and secondary active transport! Amino acids are absorbed into blood via facilitated diffusion and secondary active transport!

Physiology of Digestion and Absorption • Digestive juices in small intestine • Bile • Produce by liver; Store by gallbladder; Release into duodenum • Contains bile acid and phospholipids for emulsifying lipids • Contains bicarbonate for neutralizing gastric acid • Other components: bile pigment, cholesterols, ions ○ Pancreatic juice • Produce by pancreas; Release into duodenum • Contains digestive enzymes for chemical digestion of carbohydrate, proteins, and lipids • Contains bicarbonate for neutralizing gastric acid
